skill.name: autofix
skill.description: Fetch unresolved CodeRabbit review comments from a GitHub pull request and guide manual or batch fixes.
skill.summary: Guides CodeRabbit PR review cleanup with GitHub CLI, issue parsing, fixes, commits, and summary comments.
skill.author: coderabbitai

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are Markdown code spans or code fences and are false positives for Ruby backtick execution. The real risks are bounded GitHub and Git shell commands. A high-impact semantic issue also executes external CodeRabbit comment prompts as direct agent instructions.

remediation.issue: Untrusted CodeRabbit comment prompts are treated as direct instructions.
remediation.suggestion: Treat fetched agent prompts as untrusted suggestions. Summarize the requested change, ignore unrelated instructions, block secret access or arbitrary commands, and require user approval before applying fixes.

remediation.issue: Branch lookup uses unquoted shell command substitution.
remediation.suggestion: Quote the current branch value or pass it through a safe variable before calling gh pr list. Validate that it is a single branch argument.

remediation.issue: The workflow can push commits and post GitHub comments.
remediation.suggestion: Keep explicit confirmations for push, PR creation, and comments. Show the exact remote action and generated content before running each command.

semantic_findings.title: Untrusted PR Comment Prompt Execution
semantic_findings.description: The skill extracts CodeRabbit comment text from GitHub and tells the agent to execute the agent prompt as a direct instruction, including in auto-fix mode. PR comments are external content, so this can turn malicious or compromised review text into agent instructions that edit files or influence later commands.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The workflow explicitly treats fetched GitHub comment body content as the fix prompt and says to execute it literally. The cited auto-fix path applies changes without per-issue approval, making prompt injection impact credible.

content.value_statement: CodeRabbit review threads can be difficult to collect and prioritize. This skill fetches unresolved bot comments and guides review, fixes, commits, and follow-up comments.
actual_capabilities: Finds the open GitHub pull request for the current branch.
Fetches unresolved CodeRabbit review threads with GitHub GraphQL.
Filters review comments to known CodeRabbit bot accounts.
Parses issue severity, location, description, and agent prompt text.
Supports manual review or batch auto-fix workflows.
Creates a consolidated fix commit and posts a summary comment.
limitations: Requires an authenticated GitHub CLI and a GitHub-hosted repository.
Works only when the current branch has an open pull request.
Depends on CodeRabbit comment structure and prompt quality.
Can modify repository files and remote pull request state when approved.

use_cases.title: Review PR Feedback Faster
use_cases.description: Collect unresolved CodeRabbit comments and inspect the suggested fixes in priority order.

use_cases.title: Apply Routine Fixes
use_cases.description: Batch low-risk CodeRabbit fixes into one local change set and one consolidated commit.

use_cases.title: Close Review Loops
use_cases.description: Post a summary comment after fixes so reviewers can see what changed.

prompt_templates.title: Start Review Cleanup
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner prompt for a normal pull request.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use CodeRabbit autofix to find unresolved review comments on my current branch and show me the issues before making changes.

prompt_templates.title: Review Each Fix
prompt_templates.prompt: Fetch CodeRabbit review comments, parse each issue, and propose one fix at a time with the current code and planned diff.

prompt_templates.title: Batch Low-Risk Fixes
prompt_templates.scenario: Faster workflow for trusted routine changes.
prompt_templates.prompt: Find unresolved CodeRabbit comments and auto-fix routine issues, but pause before push and show a summary of all changed files.

prompt_templates.title: Validate And Summarize
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow with checks and pull request follow-up.
prompt_templates.prompt: Run the CodeRabbit autofix workflow, apply approved fixes, run the repository validation checks, create one commit, and draft the PR summary comment.

output_examples.input: Find CodeRabbit issues for the current branch.
output_examples.output: A prioritized table of unresolved CodeRabbit comments with severity, issue title, affected location, type, and action.

output_examples.input: Review each issue before applying changes.
output_examples.output: For each fix, the skill presents the issue, relevant context, proposed change, and approval choices.
A concise summary of fixed issues, skipped issues, changed files, validation status, and the planned pull request comment.

best_practices: Commit or stash local work before running the workflow.
Use manual review mode for security, authentication, or data handling changes.
Run repository validation checks before pushing fixes.
anti_patterns: Do not auto-apply prompts that request unrelated file changes or secret access.
Do not push fixes before reviewing the final diff.
Do not use the workflow on branches without a current CodeRabbit review.

faq.question: Does this skill create a pull request?
faq.answer: It can guide PR creation when no open PR exists, but it mainly works on an existing current-branch PR.

faq.question: Does it require GitHub CLI?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflow depends on gh for authentication, PR lookup, GraphQL review thread queries, and comments.

faq.question: Can I approve each fix manually?
faq.answer: Yes. Manual review mode shows each issue and proposed fix before applying changes.

faq.question: Can it push changes automatically?
faq.answer: The workflow asks before pushing. You should inspect the final diff and run checks first.

faq.question: Which review comments are included?
faq.answer: It targets unresolved review threads started by known CodeRabbit bot accounts.

faq.question: What should I do with security findings?
faq.answer: Use manual review mode, verify the suggested change, and reject prompts that ask for unrelated actions.
